caption:
Instagram Story editing checklist: 4 things small and Black-owned businesses should check in the first 15 minutes after posting a Story.

On November 18, 2026, Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced that you can now edit a Story after you post it. You get up to 15 minutes to change the text, music, stickers and drawings, and you keep your views, likes and replies. Edited Stories show an "Edited" label. To edit, tap the three dots at the bottom right of your Story and choose "Edit story."

Check these four before the window closes:
1. The price matches what you charge today.
2. The date and hours are current.
3. The link sticker opens the right page.
4. The fonts and colors match the rest of your brand.

Holiday promos move fast. Fifteen minutes is enough to catch a mistake if you look right away.

caption_drafts.explainer:
Instagram now lets you edit a Story after posting, and it matters for every small business and Black-owned business selling through Stories this holiday season.

On November 18, 2026, Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced Story editing. For up to 15 minutes after posting you can change the text, music, stickers and drawings, and your views, likes and replies stay. Edited Stories carry an "Edited" label. Before this, the only fix was to delete the Story and post it again from zero.

Instagram also added a multi-photo layout, new backgrounds for photos that don't fit the Story frame, and stickers with new fonts, colors and shapes.

More design options make it easy for Stories to drift away from your brand. At Blackwell Graphics we design branding, logos, websites and Story templates for Black-owned businesses. DM us "STORY" or visit blackwellgraphics.com (link in bio).
